actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.description: Transitions to advance; the action is applied at every tick
inputs.name: ticks

inputs.description: The action applied at each tick, shaped by the environment's action space
inputs.name: action

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.description: Seed of the environment's random generator
inputs.name: seed

actions.name: reset

actions.description: Set the seed used by the simulated world's random number generators for subsequent steps, without resetting the world. The accepted seed is echoed in the receipt.

inputs.name: seed

facts.text: h1-stand-v0 is registered by the loop that registers one <robot>-<task>-v0 environment for every robot and task, with entry point humanoid_bench.env:HumanoidEnv and the task's max_episode_steps
The environment id h1-stand-v0 is documented in the benchmark's environment list
The H1 robot has dof 26
The Stand observation space is a Box from -inf to +inf with shape (robot.dof * 2 - 1,)
The observation concatenates qpos and qvel into one flat vector
HumanoidEnv replaces the controller space with a Box from -1 to 1 of the model's actuator shape
The model path is built as envs/{robot}_{control}_{task}.xml under the assets directory, so h1-stand-v0 loads envs/h1_pos_stand.xml
The registration loop uses control pos for every robot except g1 and digit
The h1_pos model has 19 position actuators in its actuator block
The stand model's MuJoCo timestep is 0.002 s
Task.frame_skip is 10, so one environment step advances 10 physics frames
Task.step calls do_simulation with frame_skip
The default episode limit is 1000 steps
The Stand task sets _move_speed = 0 and success_bar = 800
The stand reward is small_control * stand_reward * dont_move
The episode terminates when the root height qpos[2] is below 0.2
Task.step always returns truncated=False; truncation is not performed by the task
HumanoidEnv.step delegates to self.task.step(action)
A reset restores the keyframe, adds uniform noise of +-randomness to qpos and returns the task's reset observation
The default reset randomness is 0.01
seed(seed) calls numpy.random.seed(seed)

determinism.notes: the upstream reset draws from numpy's seeded generator, so one seed and one action sequence repeat a trajectory; this package's fake draws its start noise from Python's random.Random, so the same seed gives a different trajectory on the fake and upstream

gaps: the deployed model is MuJoCo rigid-body dynamics with contacts (F1), but the fake backend is a pure-Python analytic stand-in: it models no contacts, actuator forces, sensors or contact noise, and its numeric constants are placeholders, not the model's

the fake does not reproduce the keyframe start state or the upstream numpy random stream: reset draws Python random.Random noise for a repeatable stand-in, so a seed gives different states than upstream
the fake does not model the stand reward, the 0.2 m termination height or the 1000-step episode limit; it returns terminated=False and truncated=False
no physical device is modelled and the benchmark was never validated against one
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0, ticks advance simulated time by timestep_ms only
snapshot and restore are not offered: the environment exposes no get_state or set_state

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: after an e-stop the runtime refuses step and reset until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch, and the last world state stays readable
